transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Weak suction on a Shark is almost always a clogged filter or a blockage, both free to fix. Work through these in order:

## 1. Wash the pre-motor filters (most likely culprit)
• Remove the dust cup and open the lid. Inside you'll find a foam filter and a felt filter.
• Rinse them under cold water only (no soap) until the water runs clear.
• Let them air-dry for at least 24 hours before refitting. Putting them back damp can damage the motor.
• Shark recommends doing this roughly monthly, so if it's never been done, this is probably your problem.

## 2. Check the post-motor (HEPA) filter
• This sits behind a cover on the main body, usually near the bottom front.
• Tap out the dust, rinse if it's washable, and dry fully. It needs cleaning less often (about once a year), but it can choke suction when clogged.

## 3. Find the blockage
To pinpoint where suction drops off:
1. Turn the vacuum on and feel suction at the end of the hose, with the wand detached.
2. Attach the wand and feel at its end.
3. Then check at the floorhead.

Wherever suction suddenly drops, the blockage is just before that point. Common spots:
• The hose, especially at the bends. Drop a coin through, or straighten it and look through it.
• The inlet on the dust cup
• The neck/joint of the floorhead, where it connects to the wand. There's often an access door here.
• Inside the wand. Look through it against a light.

## 4. Other quick checks
• Hose: look for splits or cracks. A small tear kills suction and replacement hoses are cheap.
• Seals: make sure the dust cup clicks in firmly and its rubber seals aren't cracked or packed with dust.
• Brushroll: remove it and check it spins freely. Even with anti hair wrap, string and threads can jam it.
• Dust cup: if the fine mesh/cyclone section inside is caked in dust, rinse it out (and dry it fully).

## 5. Check your warranty
If none of that works, Shark UK offers up to a 5-year guarantee on registered machines, so yours may well still be covered. Check your registration on the Shark website or contact their support before buying a new one.

I'd bet on the filters or a blockage in the floorhead neck. Those two account for the vast majority of "sudden weak suction" cases.

Never washed the foam and felt filters, didn't know they were there. The felt was caked with fine dust. I washed them in lukewarm water and left them 24 hours to dry. Suction is back to like new. No burning smell or overheating either.

Great result! A caked felt filter is the classic cause, and it's the one most people don't know about.

To keep it that way:
• Wash the foam and felt filters about once a month, more often if you have pets or are vacuuming lots of fine dust (plaster, flour, etc.). A phone reminder helps.
• Stick to cold or lukewarm water, no soap and never hot, which can shrink or warp the filters.
• Always dry them fully, 24 hours minimum, as you did.
• Consider a spare set of filters. They're inexpensive, so you can swap in a dry set straight away and not be without the vacuum while the others dry.
• Clean the post-motor (HEPA) filter about once a year. Now's a good time to check it if you haven't.
• Replace the filters if they start looking worn, thin or torn, or if they stay discoloured and suction doesn't fully recover after washing.

No burning smell or overheating is a good sign the motor hasn't suffered from the clog.
